name: entropy-coded-bf16-hostile-codec
written_before: any code. The baseline below was MEASURED by reading the rung-1 merge (f92fac65) and by running the codec module's tests in a fresh worktree on that commit — never forecast. Predictions are about the transition only.
the_claim: A representation that violates LARQL's historical mmap / random-access assumptions — one stream, sequential access, content-dependent size — becomes EXECUTABLE through registration and honest planning, without bending the contract rung 1 extracted. The decisive result is not compression ratio or speed. It is whether the eight properties below hold with the trait's surfaces byte-identical, and if any of them cannot hold without a contract change, that change IS the finding — reported, never smoothed over locally.

why_this_codec_is_hostile.one_stream_whole_object: the tensor's rows are concatenated in row-major order and coded as ONE zlib stream; no row can be reached without inflating every row before it
why_this_codec_is_hostile.size_is_an_instance_property: the stored byte count depends on the values, not the shape — the same shape stores fewer bytes for a repetitive tensor and MORE bytes than raw bf16 for a noise tensor (zlib framing + stored-block overhead)
why_this_codec_is_hostile.no_direct_kernel_is_possible: nothing can multiply against a deflate stream; the only realization is decode-to-f32, so 'representable but no kernel' is forced structurally, not chosen
why_this_codec_is_hostile.what_it_probes: every place the contract or its consumers assumed bytes = f(shape), row = offset arithmetic, or 'validate by length'

the_codec_as_it_will_be_declared.label: BF16_ZLIB

identity.note: Names the WIRE FORMAT (RFC 1950 framing over RFC 1951 deflate, Adler-32 trailer) and the element grid. It must never name flate2, miniz_oxide, zlib-the-library or any provider; the identity is checkable as a string.

the_codec_as_it_will_be_declared.streams: [VALUES] — one stream, so bind_packed's DEFAULT serves it; no override
the_codec_as_it_will_be_declared.extents: one terminal certificate. bits_per_weight = 16.0, documented as the SUPREMUM a zlib stream over bf16 asymptotically never exceeds (stored blocks cost 5 bytes per 65535); the achieved rate is an instance property, like fidelity. radius None.
the_codec_as_it_will_be_declared.stored_bytes: certificate_at(extent) FIRST (so depth 1 refuses ExtentUnavailable exactly as every terminal codec does), then REFUSES: the stored size of an entropy-coded tensor is a property of the instance, not of its shape — read the length the container records. This needs a refusal that names that remedy; see predicted_contract_touch.
the_codec_as_it_will_be_declared.validate: checks the zlib header (CMF method 8, FCHECK) and non-emptiness. It CANNOT check length from shape and does not pretend to; length is judged at decode.
the_codec_as_it_will_be_declared.decode_rows: inflates from the stream start through the end of the requested range — a non-prefix range a..b pays for rows 0..b, which is what Sequential means and is stated in the doc comment — then widens rows a..b to f32 through the same bf16 widener BF16 uses (operands.rs:497 arm "BF16"; no new arm). Truncated stream, Adler-32 mismatch, or a stream that inflates to a length other than rows*k*2 on a whole decode: refused as CodecError::Decode naming the tensor and the label.
the_codec_as_it_will_be_declared.decode_residency: ResidencyProfile::DECODED_F32 (TransientDecoded, 4 bytes/weight) — the same profile as every decode realization; the compressed SOURCE touch is the container's recorded length, observed, not declared (the profile prices resident image, for every codec, at baseline).
the_codec_as_it_will_be_declared.accelerations: EMPTY. Positively: no PhysicalProjectionPlan can consume it.
the_codec_as_it_will_be_declared.encoder: NOT part of the trait, and not added to arena.rs. Test code carries `encode_bf16_zlib(values)` via flate2 for the shared fixture table and the witness container; the lossless claim is proved against a stream produced by a FOREIGN encoder (Python zlib) checked in as a Rust const module generated by scripts/gen_bf16_zlib_fixture.py.

properties.baseline: No codec decodes through an external coder; BF16 widens in place.
properties.intervention: decode_packed over a zlib stream returns f32 whose to_bits() equal (bf16_unit as u32) << 16 for every element of the SOURCE image — compared as bits, so -0.0, subnormals, inf and NaN payloads are judged, not approximated.
properties.witness: W1 foreign fixture; W2 shared fixture table; W3 end-to-end.
properties.falsifier: any element differs in bits; or the foreign stream fails while the flate2-encoded stream passes (provider dependence).

properties.property: Sequential access only; arbitrary row access is refused by capability name, before any byte is read, in the preflight that binds operands to a prepared plan.
properties.baseline: No consumer calls CodecCapabilities::require. The packed-bank loader (experts.rs:428/470) reads the bytes and then refuses a foreign dtype BY DTYPE NAME. The op-plan builder never reads a dtype.
properties.intervention: The packed-bank loader asks the registry for the stored dtype's capabilities and calls require(RowRandom) BEFORE load_raw. BF16_ZLIB is refused as AccessRefused { label: "BF16_ZLIB", provided: "sequential", required: "row-random" }; the store's load_count is unchanged by the refusal. A BF16 bank through the same preflight loads as before (control).
properties.falsifier: the refusal names a dtype instead of an access class; or load_count moved; or the BF16 control changes behaviour; or the check needs a new trait method.
properties.scope_note: The opplan builder stays dtype-blind in this rung. A plan-BUILD-time refusal requires the planner to consult the registry per operand — that is rung 3 (realization selection + trace), and it is stated here so it cannot later be mistaken for something rung 2 delivered.

properties.baseline: F16, Q4_K, Q6_K, Q8_0, MXFP4 declare none; contract.rs:153 pins that list exactly.
properties.intervention: accelerations() is empty; the pinned list gains BF16_ZLIB; for_resident over the loaded operand observes BlasF32 (an f32 image), never a Stored/Rebound realization.
properties.falsifier: any Acceleration is declared; or any PhysicalProjectionPlan / WeightFormat variant is added.

properties.property: Explicit decode-to-f32 + f32 reference projection selection, observable.
properties.baseline: choose_for(stored_bf16=false) → BlasF32 → WeightFormat::F32 → store.load → registry decode. The selection is real but SILENT: the only observable is ResidencyCensus.widened_f32 / compact per site; there is no requested/selected/reason record for ANY codec.
properties.intervention: Zero executor edits. The witness asserts the declaration and the observation agree: for each BF16_ZLIB operand, census.widened_f32 at its site == elements * decode_residency().bytes_per_weight (== 4 * elements) and compact == 0; the loaded weight is LoadedWeight::F32; the kernel observed is BlasF32.
properties.falsifier: the operand is classified compact; or the loader needed a change to route it; or the census and the declared profile disagree.
properties.scope_note: A named trace (requested / selected / reason / residency) is NOT added in this rung. Rung 3 owns it. What rung 2 shows is that the existing observation already agrees with the codec's declaration, so rung 3 can derive the trace from declarations rather than from dtype strings.

properties.property: Compressed source touch plus transient decoded working set — both observable, told apart.
properties.baseline: ResidencyProfile prices the RESIDENT IMAGE per weight; the source read of every decode realization (2 B/w for BF16, 4.5 bits/w for a K-quant) is not in the profile for any codec. load_raw reads exactly the recorded `len`.
properties.intervention: Source touch = load_raw(operand).bytes.len() == the tensor table's `len`, which is < 2*elements for the repetitive tensor and > 2*elements for the noise tensor. Working set = 4*elements in the census. The two numbers are asserted separately and are never equal on either witness tensor.
properties.witness: W1 (both directions of the size inequality), W3 (source vs resident).
properties.falsifier: any consumer derives the source size from shape for this codec; or the profile has to grow a field for the rung to pass (that would be a contract change → finding).

properties.property: Identical stored footprint regardless of execution realization.
properties.baseline: Stored bytes are the container's `len`; the residency policy cannot change them.
properties.intervention: The candidate container's segment bytes are byte-identical before and after execution under the production backend, and load_raw returns the same length whether the operand is subsequently widened or refused (W4). stored_bytes(shape) refuses identically in every context. The ONE consumer of stored_bytes (physical.rs:478) therefore refuses expert-bank pricing for BF16_ZLIB by name — which is correct: a fixed-stride bank presupposes a shape-derived size.
properties.falsifier: a second consumer of stored_bytes surfaces that the baseline grep missed; or a caller needs a fake size to proceed.

properties.property: Stable format ID/version independent of implementation or provider.
properties.baseline: Every identity is a constant; registry.admit refuses foreign family / future revision / disagreeing geometry.
properties.intervention: identity() is the constant above; its strings contain "rfc1950" and "bf16" and contain none of {flate2, miniz, zlib-ng, libz}; admit(identity) round-trips to the codec; revision 2 is refused AbiRevision; a stream produced by Python's zlib (a different implementation) decodes bit-exactly (W1) — provider independence in both directions.
properties.falsifier: identity changes across the rung; or the foreign stream is refused.

properties.property: No new central format match arms; ideally no change to the frozen contract.
properties.baseline: Arms listed under central_match_arms_that_must_not_grow, with variant counts: WeightFormat 7 (F32,Bf16,F16,Q8,Q4,Nvfp4,Mxfp4), PhysicalProjectionPlan 9, LoadedWeight 6, RegionFormat 12 incl. Unknown, ExpertEncoding as at f92fac65.
properties.intervention: The string "BF16_ZLIB" appears in ZERO non-test files outside represent/codec/. Every enum above keeps its variant count. registry.rs builtin() gains ONE .register line — registration is the mechanism under test, so that line is the permitted touch.
properties.witness: mechanical: `git grep -l BF16_ZLIB f92fac65..HEAD -- crates/ | grep -v -E 'represent/codec/|/tests?/'` is empty; `git diff f92fac65 -- <enum files>` shows no variant.

byte_identical: codec/mod.rs (the trait and its provided methods)

one_additive_change.what: ONE new CodecError variant for 'stored size is an instance property; read the container's recorded length'. No existing variant names that remedy — Geometry says the shape cannot HOLD the encoding, which is false here, and error.rs's own rule is that a refusal naming the wrong remedy is a defect.
one_additive_change.classification: an addition to the contract's refusal VOCABULARY, not to its surfaces. Reported as a contract change in the execution notes regardless, because the user asked for exactly that honesty; whether vocabulary growth counts against the freeze criterion is decided at the freeze, not here.

candidate_findings_recorded_not_resolved: ExtentCertificate.bits_per_weight has no vocabulary for a VARIABLE-RATE code. Declaring the supremum keeps extent.rs unchanged and is honest as a bound; whether the freeze wants a rate/bound distinction is a rung-3/freeze question. Logged.
ResidencyProfile prices resident image only; source traffic is not declared for any realization of any codec. Made visible by this codec because source and image diverge in BOTH directions. Logged.

The contract is decode-only; encode lives in arena.rs as a string table. The witness produces containers from test code, and `larql vindex3 represent` cannot emit BF16_ZLIB. Logged as scope, not fixed.
predicted_contract_touch.if_any_other_contract_file_changes: that is the headline finding of the rung — the extracted contract preserved a random-access or shape-size assumption — and the execution notes must name the assumption, the file, and the minimal change, before any code is written to work around it.

witnesses.name: foreign-encoded fixture, awkward shape, both size directions
witnesses.shape: [7, 37] bf16 (259 elements, 518 raw bytes) plus a second [3, 256] fixture for the shared table.
witnesses.content: row 0 and row 3 identical (compressible); row 1 all zeros; rows 2,4,5 LCG noise (incompressible); row 6 the special values: -0.0, +0.0, smallest bf16 subnormal, largest finite, +inf, -inf, a quiet NaN with a non-zero payload, and their negatives, padded with noise.
witnesses.streams: the [7,37] image compressed by Python 3.12 zlib 1.2.11 at level 9 (foreign); a second copy of the noise-only [3,256] image whose zlib length EXCEEDS 1536 bytes.
asserts: decode_packed bits == source bits for all 259 elements
foreign_len < 518 for the [7,37] image (repetition + zeros compress); noise_len > 1536 for the [3,256] noise image
decode_rows(2..5) bits == whole[2..5]; decode_rows(0..1) is a prefix and inflates nothing past row 0's end (asserted through the inflater's consumed-input count being ≤ the full stream)
a stream truncated at 60% → Decode naming tensor and BF16_ZLIB; last Adler-32 byte flipped → Decode; a stream inflating to 517 or 519 bytes → Decode naming expected 518
stored_bytes([7,37], TERMINAL) → the new refusal; stored_bytes([7,37], depth 1) → ExtentUnavailable (extent checked first)

witnesses.name: the whole-registry gates over nine codecs
witnesses.asserts: every test under codec/tests passes with BF16_ZLIB in the fixture table; exactly the six functions above change, each by weakening a universal quantifier that encoded random access or shape-derived size; every other function is byte-identical (git diff).

witnesses.name: end-to-end execution through registration alone
witnesses.construction: encode a tiny model (the existing `hybrid_lllf_f32_model` fixture through `encode_system`), then transcode its projection tensors in test code to produce TWO containers: CONTROL with dtype BF16 (raw bf16 bytes of the rounded image) and CANDIDATE with dtype BF16_ZLIB (zlib of the SAME bytes). Every other byte of the two containers — index.json, non-transcoded tensors — is asserted byte-identical. Both rounded from the same f32 by the same function, so the images are identical by construction.
witnesses.size_condition: every transcoded matrix satisfies elements * 4 < compact_threshold_bytes(), so choose_for answers BlasF32 for BOTH containers (the control never reaches FusedBf16). The comparison therefore isolates the CODEC; it says nothing about kernels — controls before parity.
asserts: PRE-REGISTRATION CONTROL, kept permanently: a CodecRegistry::new() built from the eight rung-1 codecs refuses "BF16_ZLIB" with UnknownEncoding listing exactly those eight — proving the refusal path could have fired (a gate must be shown able to return the other answer)
with the built-in registry, the candidate container loads through PreparedOperands with ZERO edits to prepared/production/physical/weights/operands
logits for every position are BIT-EXACT (to_bits) between candidate and control under the production backend
ResidencyCensus: for each transcoded site, candidate.widened_f32 == control.widened_f32 == 4 * elements, compact == 0; and == elements * BF16_ZLIB.decode_residency().bytes_per_weight
load_raw(candidate operand).bytes.len() == the tensor table len, != 2 * elements

the F16-transcoded arm of the same model classifies identically in the census (widened_f32, compact 0) — the path is the pre-existing no-kernel path, not new behaviour (logits are NOT compared on this arm: f16 rounds differently)

witnesses.construction: a RoutedFfnOp over a packed bank whose stored dtype is BF16_ZLIB; a second over BF16 (control).
asserts: the BF16_ZLIB bank is refused with AccessRefused { label: "BF16_ZLIB", provided: "sequential", required: "row-random" } — the message names an access class, not a dtype
store.load_count() before == after the refusal (no bytes read)
the BF16 control bank loads exactly as at f92fac65 (its existing tests are untouched)
